2607.24563.title: TRACE-CTI: Auditable Post-Extraction Governance of TTP Claims with Knowledge Graphs
2607.24563.paper_summary: Security Operations Centers increasingly rely on automated mapping of Cyber Threat Intelligence reports to MITRE ATT&CK, yet extractor outputs remain fallible and are often stored without the evidence, provenance, and validation history needed to decide whether an individual mapping should be trusted. We present TRACE- CTI, a post-extraction claim-governance framework that preserves run-level Predictions, aggregates them into configuration-level GraphAssertions, materializes setup-deduplicated corroboration as ConsensusAssertions, and exposes only GraphAssertions backed by policy-compliant validation grounds. The framework retains native evidence granularity, complete extraction provenance, versioned trust decisions, and non-destructive revocation history. We evaluate TRACE-CTI on two public CTI corpora comprising 65 reports and 5,303 sentences, using a controlled 2 x 3 matrix of retrievers and generator families, incrementally ingested across six GraphVersions. All setups are incorporated without schema modification; provenance paths remain complete, operational scopes remain disjoint, and every trusted GraphAssertion has an active qualifying validation ground. Cross-generator-family setup pairs exhibit greater output diversity than same-family pairs. At the final graph state, increasing setup support from k >= 1 to six-setup unanimity raises gold-aligned precision from 25.3% to 90.6%, while recall decreases from 88.2% to 16.3%. The graph also directly answers seven questions about provenance, trust, versioning, dependency, disagreement, and review-queue that the evaluated minimal flat output cannot fully answer without enrichment or reprocessing. These results support explicit, auditable governance of extracted TTP claims; the observed corroboration trajectory is descriptive and does not establish statistical independence or a causal model-family effect.
2607.24563.paper_summary_zh: 安全運營中心越來越依賴自動化將網路威脅情報報告映射到MITRE ATT&CK，然而提取器的輸出仍然存在錯誤，且經常在缺乏證據、來源和驗證歷史的情況下儲存，這些都是決定個別映射是否值得信賴所需的。我們提出TRACE-CTI，一個後提取的主張治理框架，該框架保留運行級預測，將其聚合為配置級圖形主張，將設置去重的證實具體化為共識主張，並僅暴露由符合政策的驗證依據支持的圖形主張。該框架保留原生證據的粒度、完整的提取來源、版本化的信任決策以及非破壞性的撤銷歷史。我們在兩個公共CTI語料庫上評估TRACE-CTI，這些語料庫包含65份報告和5,303個句子，使用受控的2 x 3檢索器和生成器系列矩陣，逐步吸收六個圖形版本。所有設置都在不修改架構的情況下納入；來源路徑保持完整，操作範圍保持不重疊，每個受信任的圖形主張都有一個有效的合格驗證依據。跨生成器系列的設置對比顯示出比同系列對比更大的輸出多樣性。在最終圖形狀態下，將設置支持從k >= 1增加到六個設置的一致性，將金標準精確度從25.3%提高到90.6%，而召回率則從88.2%降低到16.3%。該圖形還直接回答了七個關於來源、信任、版本控制、依賴性、分歧和審查隊列的問題，而經評估的最小平面輸出在未經豐富或重新處理的情況下無法完全回答這些問題。這些結果支持對提取的TTP主張進行明確的、可審計的治理；觀察到的證實軌跡是描述性的，並未建立統計獨立性或因果模型系列效應。
